proposedModePenalties.status: Not validated by matched poll-mode-versus-final-results data; refuse to implement as numerical model correction

regionalCoefficients.status: Not validated; no representative county-specific survey-vs-election error dataset; no geography/religion-based penalty applied

extraTicketDrag.status: Not validated as hidden residual; double-counting risk when already reflected in Senate-specific toplines

forecast.currentMethod: Michigan: original state Senate historical poll-error correction plus a user-directed 20% transfer of the same candidate's 2026 Senate primary overpoll, applied as a nonvalidated candidate-strength sensitivity marker.
forecast.reason: A candidate-specific historical primary polling discrepancy is discounted and added as a qualitative Ervin’s Take parameter; evidence remains insufficient for a generalized Muslim Bradley, pollster-mode or county-demographic penalty.
forecast.postElectionTest: Once official Michigan Senate/governor returns exist, compare Senate and governor forecast residuals and pollster-mode matched residuals; isolate from historic Michigan partisan error, sample frame and regional covariates.

candidateStrength.label: Ervin's Take candidate-strength marker
candidateStrength.earlierContest: Michigan 2026 Democratic U.S. Senate primary, August 4
candidateStrength.rationale: Transfers only 20% of the primary polling overstatement to the general-election forecast as a judgmental, candidate-specific weakness marker. A primary is not comparable to the general electorate, and the primary included a withdrawn candidate. It is not a validated religion-related Bradley effect and is not historical statewide Senate error.
